about.title: About Unnie Note
about.description: Who makes Unnie Note, how we write in nine languages with AI, where our data comes from and how our crawler UnnieNoteBot works.
about.lead: Unnie Note is a daily news site about Korean pop culture and life in Korea, made for fans outside Korea.
about.who: We're a small independent team in Korea. Every day we cover K-pop, K-dramas, Korean entertainment, food, beauty, travel and practical guides — what fans abroad want to know about Korea. We're not affiliated with any entertainment agency, broadcaster or fan community.
about.languages: We publish in nine languages, so you can follow Korean news in your own:
about.ai: Articles are written and translated with AI from official announcements and Korean media reports. Automatic checks compare every number with the sources and stop us from copying their wording, and a draft that fails is held for human review instead of being published. The details are in our <editorial>editorial policy</editorial>.
sources: Yonhap News Agency: Korean news headlines and links from its public RSS feeds — our main source of facts.
Google Trends: what people in Korea are searching for today.
theqoo: post titles and view and comment counts from a Korean fan community, used only as a signal of what fans are reacting to.
Wikipedia page views and Wikidata: public statistics and data released under CC0.
about.photos: Photos come from official sources or Wikimedia Commons and are credited with the author, the license and a link to the original.
about.bot: To see what's happening in Korea, we fetch a small number of public pages. Our crawler identifies itself with this user agent:
botRules: It reads robots.txt first and follows it. If robots.txt can't be read (a 401 or 403 error or a bot check), it treats the whole site as off-limits.
It visits public pages only and pauses between requests. It never logs in and never hides behind rotating IP addresses.
From community sites it keeps only titles, post numbers, view and comment counts and times — never post text, images or usernames.
Nothing it collects is used to train AI models.

editorial.title: Editorial policy
editorial.description: How Unnie Note uses AI, which sources we trust, our rules for fan-community reactions, corrections and takedown requests within 24 hours.
editorial.lead: How we choose sources, use AI, handle fan-community reactions and fix our mistakes.
editorial.ai: Our articles are drafted and translated by AI from official announcements and Korean media reports, and we say so at the end of every article. Before anything is published, automatic checks run:
aiChecks: Numbers: every date, rank, sales figure or view count must match the facts collected from the sources.
Wording: if more than 25% of the text overlaps the source's wording, the draft is stopped. We report facts in our own words.
editorial.aiReview: A draft that fails a check is held for human review instead of being published.
editorial.tierOfficialText: Agencies, broadcasters, organisers and governments. Facts can be cited, with a link.
editorial.tierPressText: Yonhap and other Korean media. Facts can be cited, with a link to the report.
editorial.tierCommunityText: A signal of how Korean fans are reacting — never a source of facts.
communityRules: We store only titles, post numbers, view and comment counts and times.
We never store or re-upload post text, images or screenshots.
Reactions are summarised in our own words, with no more than two short quotes.
We always link to the original post and never show usernames.
Facts come only from official sources and the press.
Takedown requests are handled within 24 hours.
Nothing we collect is used to train AI models.
editorial.rumors: We report dating news and controversies only when there's an official statement, and we don't present claims as facts. Headlines never say more than the article. We don't retell personal stories posted in online communities.
editorial.photos: We don't use news agency photos, TV captures or social media screenshots. Creative Commons photos are shown with the author, the license and a link to the original.
editorial.corrections: If we got something wrong, use “Request a correction” at the end of the article or our <contact>contact page</contact>. We check the sources and fix the article in every language. If a report we relied on is deleted, our article comes down automatically — we recheck sources every day for 30 days after publishing.
editorial.takedown: If you wrote a post or own material mentioned on our site and want it removed, <contact>contact us</contact>. We handle takedown requests within 24 hours.
editorial.polls: Reader polls, reaction buttons and cheers are not scientific surveys. They only show how the readers who chose to take part responded. We count one vote per device and leave out bots.
editorial.rankings: Rankings are calculated by code from public data. They aren't picked by AI or by hand, and nobody can pay to change them. See <methodology>how rankings are calculated</methodology>.
editorial.ads: Ads are always labelled. Some articles show Coupang Partners banners, and we receive a commission when you buy through them. Neither changes what we write or how we rank.

privacy.title: Privacy policy
privacy.description: Unnie Note has no accounts. What we store for comments, votes and cheers (hashed, never IP addresses), analytics (Google Analytics and PostHog), what we save on your device and for how long.
privacy.lead: Unnie Note has no accounts and no sign-up. We collect as little as we can, and this page lists all of it.
privacy.noAccount: You can read, comment, vote and cheer without signing up. We never ask for your name, email address or phone number.
privacy.hash: We don't store IP addresses. When you comment, vote, react or cheer, your IP address is turned into a one-way code (an HMAC hash with a secret key) and only that code is kept. It lets us count one vote per device and stop spam, but it can't be turned back into your IP address.
hashItems: Comments: the text, the nickname shown, a hash of the edit key saved on your device (so only you can edit or delete it) and hashed codes of your IP address.

Votes, reactions and cheers: your choice, hashed codes of your IP address and browser, the page language and, for polls and cheers, the country our host detects (such as “JP”) — never the IP address itself.

Product, procedure and drama ratings: your answer (for products, also your skin type if you picked one; for procedures, whether you're curious, have had it or would pass), hashed codes of your IP address and browser, the page language and the country our host detects — never the IP address itself. We use them to show totals, such as how many readers liked a product, to count one rating per device (and one per item per day from the same internet connection) and to stop spam.

Answers such as “I’ve had it” on procedure pages can be health-related. We use them only to show anonymous totals. They're never linked to a name, email address or account, only to the hashed codes above, so we can't tell who answered.
privacy.analytics: We use Google Analytics 4 to count visits and see which articles are read. In the European Economic Area, the UK and Switzerland, analytics and ad storage are off by default (Google Consent Mode v2), so no analytics cookies are set there unless you agree in Google's consent message. Google Analytics 4 doesn't log or store IP addresses.
privacy.posthog: We also use PostHog (servers in the US) to see which pages are visited and how buttons such as votes, cheers, shares, the save heart and ratings are used (for example, which item was saved or rated and the answer chosen). It runs without cookies and stores nothing on your device. To tell visits apart, PostHog's servers turn your IP address and browser details into a one-way hash with a key that changes every day, then drop the IP address without storing it. When a page breaks or a feature fails, we also send the error details (error message, code location, page address, browser type) to PostHog so we can fix it.
privacy.ads: We show ads through Google AdSense. Third-party vendors, including Google, use cookies to serve ads based on your prior visits to this site or other websites. Google's advertising cookies let Google and its partners serve ads to you based on your visits to this site and/or other sites on the internet. In the EEA, the UK and Switzerland, ad storage is off by default and personalised ads appear only if you agree in Google's consent message. You can turn off personalised ads in <google>Google Ads Settings</google>, or opt out of other vendors' cookies for personalised ads at <aboutads>www.aboutads.info</aboutads>.
privacy.affiliate: Some articles for readers living in Korea show Coupang Partners banners. They appear only when your device's time zone is set to Korea; your browser checks this and doesn't send it to us. If you buy on Coupang after clicking one, we receive a commission, at no extra cost to you. Coupang may set its own cookies when a banner loads or when you click it. The banners don't change what we write. Shop links in our guides (such as Olive Young, YesStyle, Amazon and Klook) can be affiliate links. If you click one, that shop may set its own cookies to record that you came from us.
privacy.storageTitle: What we save on your device
privacy.storage: These are saved in your browser's storage (localStorage) and stay on your device:

storageKeys.commentKey: A random key that lets you edit or delete your comments. We keep only a hash of it.
storageKeys.commentName: The nickname shown on your comments.
storageKeys.myComments: Which comments you wrote on this device (up to 200).
storageKeys.react: The reactions you tapped on each article.
storageKeys.read: Articles you've read recently (up to 200), so we don't suggest them again.
storageKeys.install: When you closed the “Add to Home Screen” prompt.
storageKeys.localeSuggest: That you closed the language suggestion.
storageKeys.saved: What you saved with the heart (up to 300). The list is kept on this device. When you open Saved, the item IDs are sent to our server only to fetch their titles and links; we don't store them.
storageKeys.vote: Your rating for each product, procedure or drama.
storageKeys.skinType: Your skin type quiz result, so product ratings can be shown by skin type.

privacy.session: These disappear when you close the tab (sessionStorage):

sessionKeys.installSeen: The “Add to Home Screen” prompt was already shown.
sessionKeys.localeSeen: The language suggestion was already shown.
sessionKeys.celebrate: The D-day celebration was already played.

privacy.cookies: Cookies: NEXT_LOCALE remembers your language until you close the browser. Outside the EEA, the UK and Switzerland, Google Analytics sets _ga and _ga_* cookies. Google AdSense and Coupang may also set their own advertising cookies (see “Ads and affiliate banners”).
retention: Comments: until you delete them (they're erased from our database), or until we remove them or the article.
Vote, reaction and cheer records: for as long as the poll, article or ranking they belong to stays on the site.
Product, procedure and drama ratings: for as long as the item stays on the site.
Google Analytics: event data is kept for 2 months, Google's shortest setting.
PostHog: event data is kept for 1 year.
Emails you send us: only as long as we need to handle your request.
Our hosting provider keeps short-lived technical logs, which can include IP addresses, for security.
privacy.services: Vercel (hosting), Neon (database), and Google and PostHog (analytics) process data for us. Google AdSense and Coupang Partners, described above, collect data with their own cookies under their own privacy policies. We don't sell your data or hand it to advertisers ourselves. Under some US state laws, Google's personalised ads may count as “sharing”; you can turn them off in Google Ads Settings (see above).
privacy.rights: You can delete your own comments from the same device. Safari may clear what this site stored on your device if you don't visit for more than 7 days, and after that you can't delete them from that device either. You can clear everything we saved in your browser by deleting this site's data in your browser settings. If you can no longer delete a comment (include the article link) or need anything else, <contact>contact us</contact>.
